images.title: Same base, same height, same area
images.purpose: Shows that triangles on a common base with tops on a parallel line all have the same area.
images.composition: Two horizontal parallel lines; three triangles share the bottom segment BC as base.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, lots of empty space, the figure large and centred, thin dark outlines. Only the labels listed appear; no other text, no scenery, no characters. A horizontal segment BC 6 units long near the bottom, B on the left and C on the right. A long thin horizontal line l, 4 units above BC and parallel to it, running past both ends. Three triangles with base BC and top vertex on l, drawn as outlines only with no fill: the first with its top 1 unit to the left of B, outlined teal (#0072B2); the second with its top directly above the midpoint of BC, outlined amber (#E69F00); the third with its top 2 units to the right of C, outlined reddish purple (#CC79A7). A grey (#6B7280) dashed vertical line from the second top down to BC with a right angle mark. Labels: B and C at the ends of the base; l at the right end of the top line; 6 cm under BC; 4 cm beside the dashed line; 12 cm² each in clear space above line l. Check: 1/2 × 6 × 4 = 12.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Sliding the top along the parallel line changes the shape but never the area.
images.description: Shows that triangles on a common base with tops on a parallel line all have the same area.
images.context: Matches the worked example: BC = 6 cm, gap 4 cm, area 12 cm² for every position.
images.teaching_notes: Ask which triangle looks biggest, then point at the shared base and height.

image_decisions.why: Three outlines on one base make the fixed area visible; a single triangle could not show it.
